lead.headline: City Opens Office of Speculative Works
lead.dek: A new department prototypes policies before they are laws.
lead.body:
The city announced a new Office of Speculative Works tasked with piloting civic ideas as if they were products. Early programs include a seasonal residency for policy prototypes. While the office is initially funded through grants, city officials hope to demonstrate value that leads to permanent budget allocation. When there is uncertainty about how a policy will play out, prototyping allows for real-world feedback before committing to full implementation.
"We want to move beyond think tanks and public comment," said the office's director. "By treating policies as prototypes, we can learn what works and what doesn't in context." Critics worry that prototyping may delay necessary reforms or lead to half-measures. However, supporters argue that it provides a way to test ideas without full commitment, reducing risks associated with untested policies.

A public lab invites participation and makes tradeoffs visible.
